title: QuadraticFloorII: a Lean 4 formalization of fibre sums and quartic traces at conductor 8lp
description:
Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization accompanying J. S. Farland, "Quadratic floor sums II: fibre sums and quartic traces at conductor 8ℓp, formalized in Lean" (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23797605). For an odd prime p, the alternating floor sums S_{A,B,C}(p) = sum over 0 <= n < p of (-1)^floor((An^2 + Bn + C)/p) with admissible (B, C) are averages of first Bernoulli numbers of the odd characters vartheta_{p,psi} modulo 8Ap. The development proves that, weighted by psi_0(b)^2 and summed over the units b modulo A, these sums give minus the sum of B_{1,vartheta_{p,psi}} over the fibre psi^2 = psi_0^2, which is real when psi_0^4 = 1. For a prime l = 1 (mod 4), a quartic character xi modulo l and an odd prime p != l, it expresses the real part of the first Bernoulli number of Theta_{l,p} = vartheta_{p,xi}, a quartic character of conductor 8lp, and the Bernoulli number of eta_p (./l), as signed combinations of floor sums, with the case l = 13. It also proves the Euler-factor relation and the class-number shapes of the coefficients three and five, the quarter-range formula, and an elementary proof that both coordinates of B_{1,Theta_{l,p}}^{(8lp)} are even integers for every odd prime p.

Every Bernoulli number is taken at a stated modulus; at p = l, where 8lp is not the conductor (Theta_5 has conductor 40, not 200), the value equals the Bernoulli number at the conductor 8p. The folder check holds Python scripts that run numerical checks of selected statements and examples; they are not part of the formalization.

The statements are in Challenge.lean. Lean's comparator checks them against the proofs, with the definition bodies compared, and the proofs are replayed in the Lean, nanoda and con-ron kernels. No sorry, no native_decide; standard axioms only. The changes in each version are described in the release notes on GitHub: github.com/jkfarland-bot/QuadraticFloorII/releases.
notes: AI assistance: the Lean code in this record was drafted and repaired by Claude (Anthropic), an AI model, from the statements and proofs of the companion paper "Quadratic floor sums II: fibre sums and quartic traces at conductor 8ℓp, formalized in Lean" (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23797605), and compiled locally with lake. Every proof is checked by the Lean kernel, and Comparator replays the solution against the statement file under the Lean, NanoDa and con-ron kernels. The author, Joseph S. Farland, chose the scope, directed the work, and is responsible for the contents. No external human reviewer has checked the formalization.
